newsitem.title: USA: CNS sees Q1 earnings below consensus.
newsitem.headline: CNS sees Q1 earnings below consensus.

text.p: CNS Inc said Friday it expects earnings for the first quarter will be significantly below the consensus estimate of $0.23 a share reported by First Call.
CNS said an apparent inventory reduction by retailers during the months of January and February hurt the company's sales of Breathe Right nasal strips.

"Although retail sell-through of the Breathe Right strip increased in January, consistent with our expectations, it appears that retailers were reducing their inventory levels of our product as they do with other cough and cold products, which began a seasonal decline in January," Daniel Cohen, chairman, said in a statement.

While sell-through data for February is not yet available, he said conversations with a limited number of large retailers lead the company to believe that retail sales of Breathe Right strips continued to be strong.
"Our February sales to retailers were below our expectations, reflecting what we believe to be a continued reduction in retail inventory levels," he said.

He added that advertising costs during this quarter are high in order to drive the higher level of retail sales. As a result, unless retailers increase their orders substantially in March to reflect their actual sell-through to consumers, it is likely that our earnings will be below the current consensus estimate.

"This does not change our outlook for growth in sales and earnings for the year as a whole," Cohen said. "Retail sales of our product continue to be strong and we believe that retailers will eventually restore their inventory levels."

CNS said its Breathe Right nasal strip improves breathing by reducing nasal airflow resistance. It can be effective in eliminating or reducing snoring, for the temporary relief of nasal congestion, and for the temporary relief of breathing difficulties due to a deviated nasal septum.
